title: Hollow, Doubled and Weak Verb Patterns
lede: Master the high-frequency shape changes in hollow, doubled, initial-weak and final-weak verbs across useful past and present forms.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا تَتَغَيَّرُ الْأَفْعَالُ الْمُعْتَلَّةُ؟
Weak and doubled roots remain connected to one meaning, but their visible stems adapt to pronunciation and suffixes.
### Core
Produce core forms such as قُلْتُ، زُرْنَا، مَرَرْتُ and مَشَيْتُ.
### Develop
Explain when a long vowel shortens or a shadda opens.
### Stretch
Compare initial-weak and final-weak families without overgeneralising.
[callout] Communication target: Use weak verbs accurately in a connected account rather than only in tables.
## Diagnostic start
Use what you already notice, then study the full patterns.
## Hollow verbs: the middle changes shape
The middle weak radical may surface as a long vowel or as a short vowel, depending on the attached ending.
TABLE: Hollow pair | Past base | Past with suffix | Present // ق-و-ل | قَالَ | قُلْتُ / قُلْنَا | يَقُولُ // ز-و-ر | زَارَ | زُرْتُ / زُرْنَا | يَزُورُ // ق-و-م | قَامَ | قُمْتُ / قُمْنَا | يَقُومُ
[callout] Two stem shapes: the long vowel appears in forms such as قَالَ، قَالَتْ، قَالُوا . It shortens in forms whose suffix begins with a consonant: قُلْتُ، قُلْنَا، قُلْتُمْ .
[example] هُوَ قَالَ الْحَقَّ. → نَحْنُ قُلْنَا الْحَقَّ.
[ar] هُوَ قَالَ الْحَقَّ.
[ar] نَحْنُ قُلْنَا الْحَقَّ.
## Doubled verbs: merge and separate
The shadda remains in some forms and opens into two consonants in others.

TABLE: Base form | With vowel-beginning ending | With consonant-beginning ending | Present // مَرَّ | مَرَّتْ / مَرُّوا | مَرَرْتُ / مَرَرْنَا | يَمُرُّ // رَدَّ | رَدَّتْ / رَدُّوا | رَدَدْتُ / رَدَدْنَا | يَرُدُّ // أَحَبَّ | أَحَبَّتْ / أَحَبُّوا | أَحْبَبْتُ / أَحْبَبْنَا | يُحِبُّ
[callout] Why the letters separate: a shadda represents two consonants. Before a consonant-initial suffix, Arabic reveals both consonants: مَرَرْتُ , not مَرَّتُ .
## Initial and final weak verbs
A weak radical at the edge of the root can drop, return or change its written form.

TABLE: Type | Past / present | Key change | Useful forms // Initial weak | وَصَلَ / يَصِلُ | Initial و drops in many common Form I present verbs | وَصَلْتُ، نَصِلُ // Final ي-family | مَشَى / يَمْشِي | ى becomes ي before past suffixes | مَشَيْتُ، مَشَيْنَا // Final و-family | دَعَا / يَدْعُو | ا returns as و before suffixes | دَعَوْتُ، دَعَوْنَا // Final ي-family | رَمَى / يَرْمِي | ى becomes ي before suffixes | رَمَيْتُ، رَمَيْنَا
[callout/warning] Do not turn the rule into guessing. Some initial-wāw verbs keep the weak letter in other patterns. Learn the actual past/present pair used in your vocabulary.
## Pattern retrieval lines
Short oral chains make the alternations automatic without hiding the reasons.
### Hollow memory line
قَالَ — قَالَتْ — قَالُوا — قُلْتُ — قُلْنَا
Long with vowel-led endings; short before consonant-led endings.
### Doubled memory line
مَرَّ — مَرَّتْ — مَرُّوا — مَرَرْتُ — مَرَرْنَا
Shadda opens before consonant-led suffixes.
### Final weak memory line
مَشَى — مَشَتْ — مَشَوْا — مَشَيْتُ — مَشَيْنَا
The stem changes according to the ending.
### Dictionary pair rule
وَصَلَ / يَصِلُ، دَعَا / يَدْعُو
Store both tenses, not a guessed formula.
## Weak-verb misconception clinic
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
### Hollow past
✗ أَنَا قَالْتُ
✓ أَنَا قُلْتُ
The middle long vowel shortens before ـتُ.
### Doubled past
✗ نَحْنُ مَرَّنَا
✓ نَحْنُ مَرَرْنَا
The two ر consonants separate before ـنا.
### Final weak past
✗ أَنَا مَشَتُ
✓ أَنَا مَشَيْتُ
The ى becomes ي before the suffix.
### Initial weak present
✗ هُوَ يَوْصَلُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
✓ هُوَ يَصِلُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
The common pair is وَصَلَ / يَصِلُ; do not preserve و by guesswork.
## Replayable repair game
Retrieve the correct stem under time pressure, then read the explanation.
## Apply the grammar across skills
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
### 📖 Reading workshop
Read a journey blog and highlight every hollow, doubled, initial-weak and final-weak verb. Reconstruct the dictionary pair for each.
### 🎧 Listening workshop
Listen to a short group story. Each time the speaker changes from “I” to “we” or “they”, record the new verb form.
### 🗣️ Speaking workshop
Retell a past journey using قَالَ، زَارَ، مَرَّ، مَشَى and وَصَلَ. Then retell it with a different subject.
### 🛠️ Editing workshop
Correct eight weak-verb forms. For each correction, name whether the issue is shortening, shadda separation, weak-letter return or initial-letter loss.
### ✍️ Integrated production task
Write a 100–120-word account of a visit or journey. Use at least six weak or doubled verbs and include singular and plural subjects.
[callout] Model: أَمْسِ زُرْنَا مَدِينَةً قَرِيبَةً. قُلْنَا إِنَّنَا سَنَمْشِي إِلَى الْمَتْحَفِ، وَلَكِنَّنَا مَرَرْنَا بِسُوقٍ جَمِيلٍ أَوَّلًا.
[callout] Success checklist: Include two hollow verbs, one doubled verb, two final-weak forms and one initial-weak present or past pair.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Underline each target verb. Beside it, write the dictionary pair and explain the visible stem change.
## Final mastery check
Apply the patterns without relying on the table.
### Lesson mastery summary
- shorten common hollow stems before consonant-led suffixes;
- open doubled consonants where the suffix requires it;
- form common initial-weak and final-weak verbs accurately;
- use several weak-verb families in connected communication.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
